content.title: Who was voted off Survivor last night? Season 50 episode 7 recap
content.text: Updated April 9, 2026, 7:03 p.m. CTEvery player on Survivor 50 has a target on their back. They came into the landmark season with past credentials and a legacy to build upon.The majority were looking to win for the first time. But three people's targets were even bigger. They were already a winner.Of the 24 "Survivor" castaways welcomed back for season 50, Kyle Fraser, Savannah Louie and Dee Valladarees had recently won as New Era Sole Survivors.Would any of them separate themselves among fellow all-time greats and become the third two-time winner, joining legends Sandra Diaz-Twine and Tony Vlachos?Fraser, a dominant strategic force from season 48, appeared on his way to that after getting off to a strong start, but his season 50 journey ended in heartbreak due to a ruptured Achillies in the premiere. And then Louie, fresh off her season 49 win, was voted out two days later in the next episode.That left Dee Valladarees as the last winner in Fiji. She was positioning herself well and after winning an immunity necklace in the last episode she guaranteed a spot to at least the jury. But Valladarees is all about winning. Would she continue her quest or would she be next and have her torch snuffed for the first time?Here's what to know about episode 7, who was voted off and who's left on season 50:Who was voted off last night on Survivor?Dee Valladarees' attempt at becoming a two-time winner ended during episode 7.That meant that all of the prior winners are no longer in the game. She's also the first jury member, something she was looking forward to be a part of.Valladarees, the winner of season 45 following a dominant run, was voted out on an 8-4-1 vote at the largest tribal council ever for a merged tribe. Valladarees knew her time could be up and played her Shot in the Dark. But her parchment revealed her to be "Not Safe" so all the votes cast for her counted.Valladarees said in her goodbye confessional she was looking forward to being the "mayor of the jury."The 28-year-old from Miami took to Instagram after the episode aired to share her experience:"My torch got snuffed which means I’ve officially completed the Survivor circle," she wrote. "Now I get a front row seat to the chaos and a $1M vote that could change someone’s life. How lucky am I to experience every version of this game? Season 50 is special in a way that’s hard to explain."It’s 25 years of Survivor. A group of people who all came back with something to prove or something to feel. A game that pushes you in ways you can’t fully understand until you live it. So while my torch is out, I’m walking away with a full heart. See ya next week and every week after that in my cute jury outfits!"IT’S NEVER A LOSS IF THE GOAL WAS TO EXPERIENCE."What happened on Survivor last night?The episode opened with the fallout from the Blood Moon twist that saw three castaways voted out at three separate tribal councils. The biggest reactions came from Valladarees and Tiffany Ervin upset with Jonathan Young, a former ally, after they felt betrayed by voting out Kamilla Karthigesu.Coach, a central figure throughout the episode, also got involved in the spat with Dee. The Dragon Slayer was back in full force this episode.Coach later looked to recruit Rizo Velovic to his four Horseman Honor and Integrity alliance following Colby Donaldson's elimination last week. Velovic accepted the honor but he was just telling Coach what he wanted to hear.Stephenie LaGrossa Kendrick went on a journey and participated in a challenge where she had to hold her hand above her head for an hour under a water tower.If she could keep the bucket from tipping over she would earn a Steal a Vote. She successfully completed the challenge but lied about her advantage when returning to camp. However, Cirie Fields saw through her story and when she approached her about it Stephenie confessed. There might not be anyone smarter on season 50 than Fields in reading people and just forming bonds overall.Ozzy Lutsh won the immunity necklace during an endurance challenge (he battled six others immediately after his group won a separate multi-phase reward). It's Lutsh's eighth win across his four seasons, moving him closer to the all-time record held by "Boston" Rob Mariano, who has nine immunity wins.Back at camp, Coach was leading the charge on getting Dee out, but the plan was to put some votes on Tiffany Ervin as well in case Valladarees pulled out an advantage. Valladarees ended up getting a little messy in her gameplay as she told Emily Flippen about Velovic's idol, which got back to Velovic. That didn't sit well with Velovic, who went back to Fields with that information. They determined they would join in on voting out Valladarees, a former ally.The edit also appeared to indicate that Coach could be in trouble as he was getting on people's nerves. But Coach, who was showing off his Haiku game during the episode, survived for now.The same couldn't be said for Valladarees, who will now help crown the winner of Survivor 50.Oh, while she wasn't in any danger, Aubry Bracco played her Billie Eilish Boomerang Idol at tribal council as a way to remove her threat level while holding it.Stream Survivor on Paramount+Who's left on Survivor season 50?There are 13 castaways left on season 50 following episode 7 and whether they have any advantages:Aubry BraccoRick DevensTiffany ErvinCirie Fields (Extra vote)Emily FlippenChrissy HofbeckChristian HubickiJoe HunterStephenie LaGrossa Kendrick (Steal a Vote)Ozzy Lusth (Immunity Idol sent to him from Genevieve as part of the Billie Eilish Boomerang twist)Rizo Velovic (Immunity Idol sent to him from Genevieve as part of the Billie Eilish Boomerang twist)Benjamin "Coach" WadeJonathan YoungWho has been sent home on Survivor?Eleven people have been eliminated from Survivor 50 with the first 10 prior to the jury phase. Dee Valladarees, voted out during the April 8 episode, is the first member of the jury. The jury will consist of 11 people determining the winner among the final 3.Here's everyone who is no longer in the game:Jenna Lewis-Dougherty (episode 1) - voted out on Day 3Kyle Fraser (episode 1) - medical evacuation on Day 4Savannah Louie (episode 2) - voted out on Day 6Q Burdette (episode 3) - voted out on Day 8Mike White (episode 4) - voted out on Day 9Angelina Keeley (episode 5) - voted out on Day 11Charlie Davis (episode 5) - voted out on Day 11Kamilla Karthigesu (episode 6) - voted out on Day 13Genevieve Mushaluk (episode 6) - voted out on Day 13Colby Donaldson (episode 6) - voted out Day 13Dee Valladarees (episode 7) - voted out Day 15When is the Survivor season 50 finale?The Survivor 50 finale is scheduled for Wednesday, May 20. It will be a three-hour finale, starting at 7 p.m. CT.In addition to the winner being revealed, the finale will feature a live reunion with the entire cast of season 50 in Los Angeles.Every state's Survivor 50 Challenge winner is also being flown out to LA to be in the audience for the reunion.
